name: Recruitee
tagline: Applicant tracking and recruitment CRM with a hosted careers page, job multiposting and hiring team collaboration.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The part of an ATS that people actually touch daily is a pipeline board, candidate records, notes and scorecards, and that is a weekend build with no clever tricks. What breaks is everything touching the outside world: syndicating a job to Indeed, LinkedIn and local boards, an SEO-friendly careers page that does not look like a school project, inbound email parsing, calendar scheduling, and GDPR consent and retention timers that an auditor will ask about. If you are hiring for two or three roles a year and you do the sourcing yourself, the DIY version is honestly fine and you stop paying a per-seat platform tax. If you are running a hiring team where five people leave feedback and legal cares about retention, the gaps are not cosmetic. Somewhere between four and eight open roles, the SaaS quietly becomes the cheaper option.
coreLoopDIY: A local hiring app: post a role, publish a public application form, then drag candidates through pipeline stages with notes, scorecards and email templates.
requirements: Node 20 and a place to host it if the careers page needs to be public
Local disk or S3-compatible bucket for CV uploads
Manual reposting of jobs to each job board
whatYouLose: Job multiposting: one click to a dozen boards becomes a dozen logins
A careers page that ranks, converts and matches your brand without you fighting CSS
Inbound email threading, so candidate replies land in the record instead of your inbox
Scheduling that actually reads the hiring team's calendars and handles timezones
GDPR consent capture, retention deletion timers and audit trails you can hand to legal
Reporting: time to hire, source effectiveness, funnel conversion by stage
moatNotes: Job board syndication is contractual, not technical. You cannot code your way into a partner feed.
whyPeopleStillPay: Recruiting software gets bought when hiring stops being one person's side task. The moment a role needs to be visible on five boards, four interviewers need to leave structured feedback, and someone has to prove candidate data was deleted on schedule, a homemade kanban starts generating work rather than absorbing it. The other half of it is that recruiters are not the ones who would maintain the DIY build, and the person who would has a day job.
notes: The pipeline is easy, the plumbing is not. Build it if you hire occasionally, buy it if hiring is a function.
prompt:
Build a self-hosted applicant tracking app for a small team. Local-first, no SaaS accounts.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Next.js 15 (App Router) with TypeScript and Tailwind
- SQLite via Prisma, file at ./data/ats.db
- CV uploads written to ./data/uploads, served through an authenticated route
- Single shared password from ADMIN_PASSWORD in .env, cookie session, no user accounts or OAuth
- Nodemailer using SMTP_* vars in .env for outbound candidate email

In scope:
1. Jobs: title, department, location, employment type, markdown description, status (draft, open, closed), public slug.
2. Public careers pages at /careers listing open jobs and /careers/[slug] with an application form: name, email, phone, LinkedIn URL, cover note, CV upload (pdf/doc/docx, 10MB cap), and a required data-processing consent checkbox that is stored with a timestamp.
3. Candidates: one record per application, linked to a job, with source field (free text), status timestamps, and an internal activity timeline.
4. Pipeline: per-job kanban with configurable stages, default Applied, Screen, Interview, Offer, Hired, Rejected. Drag and drop, persisted stage order and position.
5. Notes and scorecards: threaded internal notes plus a scorecard with 1-5 ratings on named criteria per job and a free text summary. Reviewer is a name typed in, not a real user.
6. Email templates with {{candidate_name}} and {{job_title}} placeholders, send from the candidate page, log every send in the timeline.
7. Search and filters across candidates: job, stage, rating, keyword over name and cover note.
8. GDPR helpers: retention days per job, a page listing candidates past retention, and a hard-delete action that removes the row and the uploaded file.
9. Export: CSV of candidates for a job.
10. Seed script with two jobs and eight fake candidates so the board is not empty on first run.

Explicitly out of scope, do not stub or fake:
- Job board syndication, LinkedIn or Indeed posting, resume parsing, AI matching
- Inbound email ingestion, calendar scheduling, real multi-user permissions, analytics dashboards beyond the CSV

Deliver a README covering .env vars, prisma migrate, seed, dev and a note that the public careers routes are the only unauthenticated pages. No telemetry, no external API calls except SMTP.
